newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine teachers strike ends with more violence.
newsitem.headline: Argentine teachers strike ends with more violence.

text.p: Argentine teachers held a nationwide strike on Monday to protest the death of a young woman at a rally in the southern province of Neuquen last weekend that turned into a battle with paramilitary police.
"The sole cause of this strike is the death of a comrade in Cutral-Co and the repression," said Marta Maffei, head of the national teachers' union CTERA.
Later on Monday, tens of thousands of people held a rally in the capital's historic Plaza de Mayo to protest against the death of the 24-year-old woman on Saturday.

Some violence was reported at the end of the rally when hooded youngsters ransacked the Buenos Aires offices of Neuquen authorities and smashed windows of shops. Local news agencies said six people were arrested.
The rally capped a nationwide teachers' strike in honor of Teresa Rodriguez, a mother of three who died from a gunshot wound during clashes on Saturday in Neuquen.
Rodriguez, 24, was on her way to work when she was shot in the neck during a battle between local residents backing a local teachers' strike and paramilitary police.
Witnesses and unions blamed the death on gendarmes flown to the oil towns of Cutral-Co and Plaza Huincul to break up a highway blockade by striking teachers and local residents.

A huge crowd gathered at the Neuquen cemetery on Monday for the burial of Rodriguez and the general labor confederation CGT called three one-hour strikes for Thursday to endorse the protests against police repression.
But Interior Minister Carlos Corach, fending off calls for his resignation and that of the Education Minister, insisted the shot that killed Rodriguez was not fired by police.

"The gendarmes were attacked with molotov cocktails and shots were heard," Corach said. "What must be condemned, apart from the unfortunate death of this young woman, is the use of violence and blockades of roads, the destruction of private property and stances that put people's lives in danger."
Government officials blamed infiltrators from opposition parties for the riots.
Neuquen teachers have been on strike for a month against 20 percent pay cuts but are near a deal with the province to include half-pay for each day out if they get back to work.
The teachers' ranks have been swollen by poor locals in an oil-drilling area where the privatization of state oil giant YPF five years ago left thousands jobless.
